subject: Renewal discussion: scaling runbook + telemetry handshake
messages:
From: Samantha Lowe <samantha@brightpath.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning — second quarter utilization and topology ask

Hi Jonas,

Quick context: we reviewed Q2 usage and saw a steady utilization band at ~78% sustained across weekday windows with two short peaks up to 95% for hour-long jobs. Attaching the CSV export (brightpath_util_report_Q2.csv) — the key callout is token-concurrency on our inference path, which drove tail latencies on some customer flows.

We have an upcoming renewal (BP-4982) and are evaluating two options: a modest tranche add (~15 H100-equivalent GPUs) to flatten the peaks, or converting some steady usage into a reserved pool with autoscale headroom.

Can we get a short playbook from Redwood ops: what does a safe, reversible tranche add look like, and what telemetry would you need from us to validate effective smoothing after the change? Also include lead time and any impact to current commit pricing.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call this week.

—Samantha
Samantha Lowe
Head of Infrastructure, Brightpath
ops@brightpath.ai

Attachment: brightpath_util_report_Q2.csv (text/csv, 420KB)

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: Samantha Lowe <samantha@brightpath.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — second quarter utilization and topology ask

Samantha — thanks for the data. I reviewed the CSV and the sustained 78% band aligns with what our telemetry-based models flag as a risk window for tail-latency incidents when peak concurrency hits ~90%+.

High-level plan (proposal):
- Short-term reversible tranche: add 12 H100-equivalent slots into a dedicated pool for 90 days as a safety buffer (minimal infra migration).
- Telemetry handshake: require 7 days of pre-change 1-minute granularity metrics (token throughput, active concurrency, queue depth, 95/99 latency). Post-change we’ll run 14 days of the same metrics plus prefix/KV hit rates to validate smoothing.
- Safety and fallback: automated ramp-down rule if aggregate utilization drops below 50% for 48h (to avoid wasted spend).
- Commercial ask: propose a short-term amendment (90-day committed tranche) priced at a reduced overage rate; final pricing to be confirmed by Kimberly.

Operational lead times: we can spin the tranche in 5 business days after contract amendment + payment terms. If you want co-located placement (same region/cluster) we’ll need 7–10 business days for pinning.

I’m happy to sketch the SRE runbook (playbook) here; looping Karthik for ops capacity details and Kimberly for contract/price. Would you be available for a 30-minute call Thursday 10:00 PT?

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive — Dedicated Capacity, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_proposed_tranche_schedule.pdf (application/pdf, 120KB)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, Samantha Lowe <samantha@brightpath.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 08:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — second quarter utilization and topology ask

Thanks for the context. A few operational specifics to add to Jonas's runbook: 

- Tranche sizing: 12 H100-equivalent GPUs should reduce observed peak concurrency by ~18–22% given your shard profile (we modeled using your CSV). If you prefer headroom vs. cost, we can size to 16 GPUs for ~30–35% effective peak reduction.
- Binning and routing: we recommend routing the heaviest models to the new tranche and keeping lighter traffic on existing pools; that reduces cache cold-starts.
- Telemetry collection: we’ll need a 7-day pull of: live token throughput (1-min), active sessions, queue depth, p50/p95/p99 latency, and model shard mapping. If Brightpath can expose a short-lived metrics endpoint or grant a read-only CloudWatch/Datadog role we’ll ingest automatically.
- Rollout steps (ops):
  1) Precheck: validate KV cache warming plan and model placement (day -2)
  2) Cutover: route 15% of traffic to tranche for first 4 hours, monitor latencies and error rates
  3) Ramp: if stable, step to 50% after 12 hours, then full shift over 48 hours
  4) Post-validate: 14-day telemetry comparison and cost reconciliation

Risk notes: prefix cache churn is the largest near-term failure mode — expect some transient p95 increases during the first few hours unless we pre-warm. We can add a simultaneous pre-warm job as part of the cutover.

I’ll align runbook tasks with our SRE team once we have a confirmed tranche size.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Engineering Manager, Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Samantha Lowe <samantha@brightpath.ai>, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 14:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — second quarter utilization and topology ask

Samantha — appreciate the detail and the CSV. Commercial side: we can support the 90-day reversible tranche at the following terms:

- Option A (conservative): 12 H100-equivalents, 90-day amendment, 10% overage discount on the tranche rate; immediate add-on charge prorated for the first 30 days.
- Option B (headroom): 16 H100-equivalents, 90-day amendment, 15% overage discount; includes one-time onboarding credit of $10k to offset pre-warm work.

If Brightpath wants to convert to a longer reserve after the 90 days we can roll into a 12-month commit with a blended rate and an SLA uplift. For the HubSpot deal BP-4982 I’ll draft an amendment and payment terms and share a DocuSign link.

Next steps: please confirm preferred option and whether you grant a read-only metrics role (or will share logs). If you confirm Option B and telemetry access by EOD Monday, we’ll queue the tranche for provisioning with a targeted spin-up date of Jun 21 (10 business days).

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Director, Commercial Sales, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
